\begin{corollary}[Intrinsic player views]\label{gen:cor:views}
Every idempotent operation in the full role-switching language acts
compositionally on each of the $K+1$-state player views

 q_k(S)=
 \begin{cases}
 \pv,&k\in S,\\
 a_i,&S=\{i\},\ i\ne k,\\

 \end{cases}
\]

irredundant: none of its player views can be omitted.
\end{corollary}

claims.title: Two-policy classification
claims.statement_latex:
\begin{corollary}[Two-policy classification]\label{selective:cor:two-policies}
Fix $K\geq3$ and two policies $D,E$. Equation validity for
$\{\del,R_D,R_E\}$ has the following complexity:
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{ll}
\toprule
Policies & Complexity\\
\midrule
Comparable by inclusion & Polynomial\\
Incomparable and disjoint & coNP-complete\\
Incomparable and overlapping, every atomic pattern unique & coNP-complete\\
Incomparable and overlapping, some atomic pattern repeated & Polynomial\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
In the last two rows a pattern is one of the nonempty regions
$D\cap E$, $D\setminus E$, $E\setminus D$, and
$I\setminus(D\cup E)$; it is unique when that region is a singleton.
\end{corollary}

claims.title: Finite-family dichotomy
claims.statement_latex:
\begin{theorem}[Finite-family dichotomy]\label{selective:thm:families}
For fixed $K\geq3$ and $\mathcal D$, equation validity for native tree
terms in $\{\del\}\cup\{R_D:D\in\mathcal D\}$ is polynomial exactly
in the following cases, with coNP-completeness in all other cases:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal P$ is a chain under inclusion; or
\item $\mathcal P$ is intersection-closed and some pattern has
      multiplicity at least two.
\end{enumerate}
In the second case, any observer with a repeated pattern is
equation-complete, and a failed comparison has a singleton-or-pair
countervaluation. The classification criterion itself is polynomial
in an explicitly listed family and role set.
\end{theorem}

claims.title: Uniform-profile observation
claims.statement_latex:
\begin{proposition}[Uniform-profile observation]\label{game:prop:uniform-observation}
Let $f[x]$ be any unary owned-choice context and $G$ any closed component.
The winners of ordinary SPE profiles that use one and the same full SPE
profile of $G$ in every copy are exactly
\[
 U(f)(\den{G})=\bigcup_{g\in\den{G}}f(\{g\}).
\]
Thus uniform copies preserve the ordinary observation at $S$ precisely
when $f(S)=\bigcup_{g\in S}f(\{g\})$.
\end{proposition}

claims.title: Uniform copies suffice
claims.statement_latex:
\begin{proposition}[Uniform copies suffice]\label{game:thm:uniform}
Fix pairwise distinct $r,s,t$, a full SPE profile $p$ of $G$,
and a full SPE profile $q$ of $H$, with
winners $g,h$. In
\[
  (G\ch r H)\ch t(G\ch s H),
\]
use exactly $p$ in both copies of $G$ and exactly $q$ in both copies of
$H$. As the three outer actions vary, the winners of ordinary SPE
profiles are exactly $\{g,h\}$. Therefore the winners of ordinary SPE
profiles satisfying this copy-equality condition are
$\den{G}\cup\den{H}$.
\end{proposition}

claims.title: Congruence classification
claims.statement_latex:
\begin{theorem}[Congruence classification]\label{view:thm:congruences}
The congruences of $\A$ are exactly the kernels of closure operators
$c:\Pow\to\Pow$ satisfying
\begin{equation}\label{view:eq:atomclosure}
 c(\{i\})\in\{\{i\},I\}\qquad(i\in I).
\end{equation}
Equivalently, they correspond to families $\mathcal F\subseteq\Pow$
such that $I\in\mathcal F$, $\mathcal F$ is closed under nonempty
intersections when the result is nonempty, and
\[
 S\in\mathcal F,\ S\ne I,\ i\in S\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \{i\}\in\mathcal F.
\]
The closure is the intersection of all members containing the input.
\end{theorem}

claims.title: Subdirectly irreducible homomorphic images
claims.statement_latex:
\begin{proposition}[Subdirectly irreducible homomorphic images]\label{view:thm:si}
Every nontrivial subdirectly irreducible homomorphic image of $\A$ is
obtained from a nonempty proper set $S\subset I$ with closed family
\[
 \mathcal F_S=\{I,S\}\cup\{\{i\}:i\in S\}.
\]
For $|S|=1$ the quotient has two elements. For $|S|\geq2$ it has
$|S|+2$ elements: one singleton state per $i\in S$, the state $S$, and
the state $I$. In particular, every such image has at most $K+1$ elements.
The case $S=I\setminus\{k\}$ is exactly $C_k$.
\end{proposition}

claims.title: The symmetric congruence chain
claims.statement_latex:
\begin{proposition}[The symmetric congruence chain]\label{view:thm:sym}
There are exactly $K$ congruences of $\A^{\mathrm{sym}}$. They are the
kernels of
\[
 c_m(S)=\begin{cases}S,&|S|\leq m,\\I,&|S|>m,\end{cases}
 \qquad m=0,1,\ldots,K-1.
\]
Here $m=0$ gives the universal relation and $m=K-1$ gives equality.
For $1\leq m\leq K-1$, the quotient has
$1+\sum_{j=1}^{m}\binom Kj$ values. These are the restrictions to
nonempty sets of the uniform-matroid closures of rank $m+1$.
\end{proposition}

claims.title: Private-store connection
claims.statement_latex:
\begin{theorem}[Private-store connection]\label{dep:thm:connection}
For well-formed fragments $P,Q$ with matching boundary and input family
$W$, connection has the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Every execution preserves dependent typing and each stored witness.
Its boundary store belongs to $W_P$, and
\[
 \mathsf{Run}_{P;Q}(\sigma,\tau;\rho)
 =\mathsf{Run}_Q(\tau;\mathsf{Run}_P(\sigma;\rho)).
\]
The stores retain all intermediate bound values.
\item There is a canonical bijection
\[
 \mathsf S_i(P;Q;W)\cong
 \mathsf S_i(P;W)\times\mathsf S_i(Q;W_P).
\]
It preserves every decision at every legal view, and carries whole-player
unilateral deviations to pairs of component deviations.
\item Connection is associative, with the empty fragment as unit,
up to consistent bound-name renaming and the displayed strategy
bijections. Rebracketing preserves histories, dependent answer families,
observation partitions, and execution.
\item Sealing certificates compose when the marked dependency set at
the end of the first fragment is passed unchanged to the second.
The two-execution hiding theorem therefore holds across this private
boundary for implementations satisfying those certificates.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

claims.title: Passing relation
claims.statement_latex:
\begin{lemma}[Passing relation]\label{owner:lem:passing}
Let $(C,\del,h)$ be conservative and satisfy $\Sigma$. Its reset
reduct is the forest order of \cref{reset:thm:forest}. Write
$v\parallel w$ for incomparability. Except on triples
\[
 x<b,\qquad z\parallel b,\qquad z\parallel x,
\]
with root $x$ and side arguments $b,z$ in either order, $h$ equals
$h_0(x,y,z)=(y\del x)\del(z\del x)$.
On an exceptional triple it returns either $x$ or $b$.

For nonminimal $b$ and $z\parallel b$, define $E(b,z)$ by
$h(x,b,z)=b$ for some $x<b$. Then ``some'' can be replaced by
``every'', and
\begin{align}
 b\leq c,\ z\parallel c,\ E(b,z)&\ \Longrightarrow\ E(c,z),
       \label{owner:eq:passing-up}\\
 z\leq z',\ z,z'\parallel b&\ \Longrightarrow\
       \bigl(E(b,z)\Longleftrightarrow E(b,z')\bigr).
       \label{owner:eq:passing-constant}
\end{align}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[A typed cover]\label{core:lem:typed-upper-clone-cover}

$A_e(C)\in\operatorname V(\mathbf C_K)$.

claims.title: Unary polynomial normal forms
claims.statement_latex:
\begin{proposition}[Unary polynomial normal forms]
\label{core:prop:unary-polynomials}
For $K\geq3$, the unary polynomial functions of $\mathbf C_K$ are
the constant functions and precisely the functions
\begin{equation}\label{core:eq:unary-profile}
 f_{U,B}(S)=
 \begin{cases}
  \{i\}\cup B_i,&S=\{i\},\\
  S\cup U,&|S|\geq2,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 U\subseteq I,\quad B_i\subseteq U\setminus\{i\}.
\end{equation}
There are exactly
\[
 (1+2^{K-1})^K+2^K-2
\]
such polynomial functions. Every unary polynomial $p$ satisfies
$p^3=p^2$, and this identity schema holds throughout
$\operatorname V(\mathbf C_K)$. The exponent two is sharp.
\end{proposition}
